method: Read-only verification of the 14 workbook rows. WebFetch first on every workbook URL plus the statewide court portals (Maryland Judiciary Case Search, mdcourts.gov/data and /mdec/publiccases, Virginia GDC Online Case Information System, VA OCIS, DC Courts case search); mdcourts.gov / courts.state.md.us / dccourts.gov answer 403 (Akamai) to WebFetch, so src/scrapfly_browser.py rendered the Case Search landing page (upstream 200) before Scrapfly throttled the account (429) and further Scrapfly attempts were stopped. WebSearch located replacement pages and the Maryland CAPTCHA and eviction-shielding statements; the Maryland daily statewide 'AOC - Cases Filed Report' PDF was verified by parsing the copy already on this machine (Divorce Cases/file2026-08-27.pdf, pulled by the MD Cases scheduled task) rather than re-downloading it. No accounts created, no forms submitted, no CAPTCHA solved, no Firecrawl, no src/scripts run.

baltimore_county_md.changed_vs_workbook: Case Search relaunched 2026-03-14 as the unified 'Maryland Judiciary Case Search & Record Portal' (Case Portal 1.1, Odyssey-based, Sign In / Register plus an I-Agree disclaimer gate and CAPTCHA); the workbook's claim that no bulk extraction exists is wrong: the daily statewide AOC Cases Filed Report PDF lists every District Court LT filing with the landlord as plaintiff.
baltimore_county_md.notes: The scraper route is the daily PDF, not the portal: file2026-08-27.pdf held 2,037 'Failure to Pay Rent' plus 6 'Tenant Holding Over' and 10 'Wrongful Detainer' entries statewide, each as 'D-0xx-LT-26-nnnnnn | <Landlord> vs. <Tenant> | case type | file date', sectioned by District Court location (Towson, Essex, Catonsville for this county), so 12 months of PDFs aggregated by plaintiff name yields the multiple-eviction landlord list directly; LT entries carry no property address (only criminal entries print a defendant address), so the address comes from a per-case Case Search lookup behind the CAPTCHA. Gotcha: mdcourts.gov is Akamai-fronted (403 to WebFetch, Scrapfly ASP failed), but the MD Cases scheduled task already downloads the file daily with plain PowerShell from a residential IP. Under SB 19 (eff. 2024-10-01) FTPR cases that do not end in removal are shielded within 60 days of judgment, so capture at filing, not later.

fairfax_va.changed_vs_workbook: Portal is reCAPTCHA-gated (captchaVerification.do; every search page redirect-loops without the gate cookie), which the workbook's 'Medium' access does not mention. The statewide OCIS (eapps/ocis) that the vacourts court pages now point to covers only criminal/traffic for GDC; civil unlawful detainer stays in the per-court gdcourts system.
fairfax_va.notes: Scraper must clear the reCAPTCHA once per session, then query ONE court at a time (FIPS 059) in the Civil Division: name search (plaintiff or defendant, '*' wildcard, min 2 chars) needs a landlord name up front, so the enumeration route is the Hearing Date search per court day, keep GV-prefixed civil cases with an unlawful detainer hearing type, and GROUP BY plaintiff across 12 months. No case-type filter exists; civil is identifiable only by the GV case-number prefix. Bulk: none public at case level (OES publishes only Power BI aggregates and monthly filings PDFs), and Va. Code 16.1-69.54:1 lets OES supply aggregated data reports that 'shall not include the name ... of any party' and may not be redistributed, so the statutory bulk route cannot name landlords. No terms-of-use text about automated access appears on the gdcourts pages.
